pairs.why: B is built like a real calculator with printed digits and operator symbols, like the real card; A's keys are blank, so it reads as a generic prop, even though its dark-blue keys match the real colour better.
A's finish is softer and less saturated, and its proportions and dull-gold trim sit closer to the real chest; B is glossier, more contrasty and over-decorated with oversized gems.
B is built like a real stave barrel with hoops, like the real wooden props; A has a knobbed lid that turns it into a cookie jar, and its finish is glossier and more toy-like.

A matches the real backpack's construction: a lime flap with two buckled straps, a lower pocket with two straps, and puffy side pockets; B simplifies the front pocket to one strap and adds a brown base the real one doesn't have.
B's straight-edged blades with a dark insert and smooth yellow finish match the real fins; A's wavy blade tips and thick orange rim make it look like a rubbery toy.
B has more believable locomotive construction (connecting rods, boiler bands, tender) at a detail level like the real bus and bike; A is chunkier and more simplified toy-like.
A hangs flat on the striped wall and casts a soft shadow, as the real wall clock does; B stands on a floor like a desk object, which changes how the object is staged and built.
Same pair as p205: A is a wall clock lying against the wall with a cast shadow like the real card, while B is a standalone clock sitting on a ground plane.
